newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche Telekom shares issued at 28.50 dmk.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche Telekom shares issued at 28.50 dmk.

text.p: Shares in Deutsche Telekom AG, being issued to investors from Monday in Europe's largest ever stock listing, will be priced at 28.50 marks each, the company's chief executive Ron Sommer said on Sunday.

In a statement issued at a news conference, Sommer said the issue, which has whipped up feverish interest among usually cautious German investors, had been oversubscribed at least five times and would raise total proceeds of about 20 billion marks.
Of the total issue of 713 million shares, 33 percent had gone to investors outside Germany, where interest had also been very strong, Sommer said.
"Foreign investors took up around 33 percent of the floated shares. The demand was many times this and represented a volume of more than 30 billion marks," he said.
Of the total issue, more than 50 percent was likely to be taken up by institutional investors, Sommer said, noting however that there had been a huge level of interest from private investors.
These small shareholders, who have been wooed by Telekom in blanket advertising campaign, would be guaranteed a minimum of 100 shares, he said.
Telekom shares, which will immediately take a dominant role in Germany's 30-share DAX index, will begin trading on stock markets around the globe from November 18.
